submission.justification:
Sensor-T3 at 150 μm thickness is recommended as the optimal configuration for the innermost pixel layer, achieving the best possible single-hit spatial resolution of 9.063 μm while meeting all mandatory requirements.

KEY RATIONALE:

1. BEST SPATIAL RESOLUTION: Sensor-T3 delivers 9.063 μm resolution at 150 μm thickness, representing a 33% improvement over the only viable alternative (Sensor-T2: 13.535 μm). This directly addresses the primary goal of achieving the best possible spatial resolution.

2. RADIATION HARDNESS COMPLIANCE: With 98.5% hit efficiency at the end-of-life fluence (2×10¹⁶ neq/cm²), Sensor-T3 exceeds the mandatory 97% threshold with a comfortable 1.5 percentage point margin.

3. OPTIMAL THICKNESS: The 150 μm thickness represents the fundamental optimum identified through systematic simulation, balancing charge collection efficiency against charge diffusion and multiple scattering effects. Both viable technologies (T2 and T3) converged on this same optimal thickness.

4. TECHNOLOGY SCREENING: Sensor-T1 was eliminated early despite having superior unirradiated resolution (6.0 μm) because it achieved only 82% hit efficiency at end-of-life fluence, falling critically short of the 97% requirement by 15 percentage points.

This recommendation provides the HL-LHC inner tracker with the highest precision tracking capability while ensuring robust operation throughout the detector's lifetime in the extreme radiation environment.
